::: {.callout-important}
## Watch. Do not type.
Thirty minutes, three faculty, one complete workflow. The full script is on
this page. You will have it afterwards. Watching how someone experienced
moves between console, script and document is the point; transcribing it is
not.
:::

## What you will see

An empty folder becomes a rendered report in half an hour, including the
mistakes. Faculty will deliberately leave the errors in: the misspelt column,
the forgotten `na.rm`, the join that duplicates rows. Watching an expert
recover from an error is more instructive than watching one avoid it.

| Minutes | Step | Led by |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 | Project setup, folder structure, `.Rproj` | Biju Soman |
| 5–12 | Import, inspect, clean; the join that goes wrong | Gurpreet |
| 12–20 | EDA and the figure, built layer by layer | Gurpreet |
| 20–26 | `gtsummary` table, model, into the `.qmd` | Arun Mitra |
| 26–30 | Render to HTML and Word; the reproducibility test | Arun Mitra |

## The pipeline

```{r}
#| eval: false
# 01_analysis.R ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Flipped classroom and knowledge gain: complete workflow
# Run with a clean session: Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + F10, then source this file.

library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)

# 1. Import -------------------------------------------------------------------
students <- read_csv("data/meded_students.csv")
osce     <- read_csv("data/osce_stations.csv")

glimpse(students)
stopifnot(nrow(students) == 240)   # fail loudly, early

# 2. Derive -------------------------------------------------------------------
osce_summary <- osce |>
  group_by(student_id) |>
  summarise(
    osce_total    = sum(score),
    osce_mean     = mean(score),
    n_stations    = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(all(osce_summary$n_stations == 5))   # catch the bad join before it happens

analysis <- students |>
  left_join(osce_summary, by = "student_id") |>
  mutate(
    teaching_arm = factor(teaching_arm,
                          levels = c("Traditional lecture", "Flipped classroom")),
    attendance_band = case_when(
      attendance_pct >= 90 ~ "High",
      attendance_pct >= 75 ~ "Adequate",
      .default             = "Below requirement"
    ),
    complete_case = !is.na(posttest)
  )

stopifnot(nrow(analysis) == nrow(students))    # the join did not duplicate

# 3. Describe -----------------------------------------------------------------
n_excluded <- sum(!analysis$complete_case)
message("Excluded for missing post-test: ", n_excluded)

tbl1 <- analysis |>
  select(teaching_arm, age, sex, rural_background, attendance_pct,
         pretest, osce_total) |>
  tbl_summary(
    by = teaching_arm,
    label = list(age ~ "Age (years)", sex ~ "Sex",
                 rural_background ~ "Domicile",
                 attendance_pct ~ "Attendance (%)",
                 pretest ~ "Pre-test score",
                 osce_total ~ "OSCE total (/100)")
  ) |>
  add_overall() |>
  bold_labels()

# 4. Visualise ----------------------------------------------------------------
fig1 <- analysis |>
  filter(complete_case) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = teaching_arm, y = gain, fill = teaching_arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Traditional lecture" = "#b8860b",
                               "Flipped classroom"   = "#0f5257")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Knowledge gain (post − pre)",
       title = "Knowledge gain by teaching method",
       subtitle = paste0("n = ", sum(analysis$complete_case),
                         " with complete data")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave("output/fig1_gain.png", fig1, width = 7, height = 4.5,
       dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# 5. Model --------------------------------------------------------------------
m1 <- lm(gain ~ teaching_arm + pretest + attendance_pct + sex, data = analysis)

tbl2 <- tbl_regression(
  m1,
  label = list(teaching_arm ~ "Teaching arm", pretest ~ "Pre-test score",
               attendance_pct ~ "Attendance (%)", sex ~ "Sex")
) |>
  add_glance_table(include = c(nobs, r.squared)) |>
  bold_p()

# 6. Render -------------------------------------------------------------------
# quarto::quarto_render("report.qmd")
```

## Three habits to notice

**`stopifnot()` after every join and import.** It costs one line and turns a
silent wrong answer into a loud stop. The `n_stations == 5` check catches a
duplicated station before it inflates every OSCE total, an error that would
otherwise survive to publication looking entirely plausible.

**`factor(levels = ...)` set explicitly.** R orders factors alphabetically, so
"Flipped classroom" would become the reference category by accident. Setting
the reference deliberately means the regression coefficient answers the
question you meant to ask.

**The figure and the table are objects.** `fig1` and `tbl1` are created in the
script and referenced from the `.qmd`. Nothing is copied. Change the data,
re-source, re-render, and every number and every figure updates together.

## The reproducibility test, live

At minute 28, faculty will:

1. Delete the entire `output/` folder.
2. Restart R (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>).
3. Source `01_analysis.R`, then render `report.qmd`.
4. Show that everything comes back, identically.

If your own project cannot survive that, it is not yet reproducible, and now
you know exactly how to find out.
